thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 PROD alert: sudden p95 latency jump on runtime-service (us-west-2). Error budget burn increasing. Paging oncall. See /alerts/ALRT-789.
maria: Noted. I'm pulling traces and recent deploys. Which deploy went out ~10m ago?
jake: That was the rollout from release-2026.03.17-rc4, 10:12 PDT. I'm oncall and patching in.
oncall: Observing kernel-fallback messages on a subset of GPUs, plus batching queue length spiked. Possible scheduler change from the release.
sre-lead: Copy. Can you paste the quick logs and the anomaly window?
maria: Logs (filtered):
```
2026-03-17T17:11:58Z runtime INFO selected_kernel=fast_attn
2026-03-17T17:12:05Z runtime WARN kernel_fallback=slow_generic reason=unsupported_op
2026-03-17T17:12:06Z batching WARN queue_depth=124 latency_p95=480ms
2026-03-17T17:12:30Z telemetry ERROR client_timeouts=12
```
maria: Percentiles jumped after the rollout: p50 + 30ms, p95 + 370ms, tail spikes to ~1.2s for some routes.
lucy-cs: Any customer-facing impact? A few customer sessions reported timeouts in PROD-US-W.
jake: CS reported 3 customers with elevated request errors; no major outages but degraded UX. Lucy is reaching out.
sre-lead: Risk assessment: high for latency-sensitive routes. Root likely the new request-slicing scheduler (opt-in) in rc4 that changes batching behavior and kernel selection logic.
oncall: I can flip the feature flag to revert the scheduler. Recommended immediate mitigation: disable new_scheduler flag in prod for the affected slice, then evaluate.
maria: Can we instead do a quick rollback of the runtime deployment? Downside: rollback may evict warmed KV caches causing transient tail latencies, but it should restore previous stable kernel selection.
jake: Given customer impact and kernel fallback, I prefer kill-switch first (feature flag) — least blast radius. If that doesn't drop p95 in 5m, roll back.
oncall: Agreed. Executing flag toggle now.
```
# Command run
redwoodctl feature flag set new_scheduler false --env prod --selector=runtime-service:us-west-2 --reason "auto-mitigation latency regression"
```
incident-bot: action taken: feature flag disabled by oncall at 17:15:22Z. Tracking mitigation.
maria: Metrics after toggle (1m): p95 dropped from 630ms -> 280ms, queue_depth -> 30, kernel_fallback logs no longer appearing for most hosts.
sre-lead: Nice. Still keep an eye on throughput and error rates for next 10m. Schedule an A/B test rollback plan if any anomalies persist.
jake: CS update: Lucy reports 3 customers' sessions stabilized; two had truncated responses but no data loss. She's sending a templated note to affected customers.
lucy-cs: Sending message now: "We've observed intermittent latency and timeouts between 17:12-17:18 PDT; mitigation applied and service is stable. We're following up with root cause and timeline." :email:
oncall: I'll leave a watch for 30m and then handoff to next oncall. Maria, can you start a postmortem draft with the timeline and the flag vs rollback decision rationale?
maria: On it. I'll include graphs and the kernel selection diff from the rc4 merge.
sre-lead: Ops notes: action items — 1) revert scheduler change in next patch candidate and add unit test for kernel ops; 2) add automated safety check in rollout to detect kernel_fallback increase > X% in 5m; 3) add canary gating that monitors batching queue_depth.
incident-bot: incident severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 17:28:10Z. No further paging.
jake: Handoff to next oncall @17:45. Leaving runbook steps in #eng-oncall. Key checks: p95 < 320ms, kernel_fallback log count ~0, queue_depth < 50.
oncall: Handoff ack. Will escalate if we see reoccurrence.
maria: Drafted postmortem outline and linked traces and the PR that introduced the scheduler: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/342
lucy-cs: Notified affected customers; one wants a follow-up call. Scheduling with product.
incident-bot: Resolution note: feature flag rollback restored kernel selection and batching behavior; full rollback of runtime not required. Incident closed at 17:49:49Z. Follow-ups assigned to maria, sre-lead, and product.
